selected_mechanism.name: Data-center survey disclosure suit
selected_mechanism.definition: A state agency that holds survey responses from data centers asks the Attorney General whether public records law requires release, and then may sue in Travis County to block that release.
selected_mechanism.texas_scope: Texas, Travis County district court, responses to the Energy and Water Use Survey for data centers and virtual currency mining facilities

news_trigger.verbatim_span: files its Original Petition against Defendant Ken Paxton, in his official capacity as the Texas Attorney General

corroboration.note: Independent reporting dated October 6th, 2026 corroborates the filing; it is not used as a primary source for any layer.

layers.name: Records held
layers.function: The Commission holds facility responses to its survey, which are public information unless an exception applies
layers.actor_authority: Gov't Code Sec. 552.021 makes public information available; the petition states the survey responses are held by the Commission

layers.name: Attorney General decision
layers.function: A governmental body that withholds records must ask the Attorney General for a decision, which issues within 45 business days
layers.controlling_actor: Open Records Division of the Attorney General
layers.actor_authority: Gov't Code Sec. 552.301(a) requires the request; Sec. 552.306(a) requires a decision not later than the 45th business day

primary_source.title: Open Records Letter Ruling OR2026-038988, September 2nd, 2026

layers.name: Homeland Security exception
layers.function: The Commission claimed Sec. 418.181 covers the survey information; the Open Records Division found the claim was not shown for the submitted information
layers.controlling_actor: Open Records Division of the Attorney General
layers.actor_authority: Sec. 418.181 covers technical details of particular vulnerabilities of critical infrastructure; the ruling found the Commission had not demonstrated that for the submitted information

primary_source.title: Open Records Letter Ruling OR2026-040171, September 11th, 2026

layers.name: Declaratory suit
layers.function: A governmental body may sue only in Travis County against the Attorney General to seek declaratory relief within 30 calendar days of receiving a disclosure decision
layers.actor_authority: Gov't Code Sec. 552.324(a)-(b) and 552.325; the petition is captioned in the 200th District Court and states cause number D-1-GN-26-010018

primary_source.title: Plaintiff's Original Petition, cause D-1-GN-26-010018 (publisher mirror of Travis County filing; clerk-style stamp 10/5/2026 5:37 PM; not the District Clerk record)

chokepoint.binary_decision: Whether Sec. 418.181 makes the facility county and state regional water planning area fields confidential
chokepoint.post_decision_phrase: whether the two fields are exempt
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: After the Attorney General ruling, the only route to block release is the Travis County declaratory suit under Sec. 552.324, so this court is where the disputed exemption is decided

selected_mechanism.texas_consequence: Public access to the county and regional water planning area of Texas data centers and virtual currency mining facilities that reported to the Commission survey
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The machinery is legible. A records request reached the Commission, the Commission asked the Attorney General to decide, the Attorney General ruled on September 2nd, 2026 that the Commission had not shown the Homeland Security exception applies to the submitted information, and the Commission filed suit on October 5th, 2026. The ruling does not name the county or water planning area fields, so the petition is the only source for which fields are disputed. The petition's security argument is an allegation that the Attorney General has not yet tested in court.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Until the 200th District Court rules, whether the disputed fields stay confidential is unresolved. The record here does not say whether release is paused during the suit.

verified_facts.claim: The Commission filed its Original Petition against the Attorney General in the 200th District Court, cause D-1-GN-26-010018, stamped 10/5/2026 5:37 PM
Ruling OR2026-038988 issued September 2nd, 2026 and the Commission received it on September 3rd, 2026 (per the petition)
Ruling OR2026-038988 found the Commission had not shown the information identifies technical details of particular vulnerabilities, so it may not withhold under Sec. 418.181
Ruling OR2026-038988 orders withholding of Sec. 552.110(c) information and Sec. 552.137 personal emails and release of the remaining information
Ruling OR2026-040171 issued September 11th, 2026 and applied OR2026-038988 as a previous determination to identical information
Sec. 418.181 covers documents identifying technical details of particular vulnerabilities of critical infrastructure to an act of terrorism or a hostile act by a foreign adversary
Sec. 552.306(a) requires the Attorney General to decide not later than the 45th business day after receiving the request
Sec. 552.324(b) requires the governmental body to sue within 30 calendar days after receiving a disclosure decision

The petition seeks a declaration that the facility county and state regional water planning area fields are confidential under the Public Information Act, and states this as relief sought, not as a proven fact

The petition lists the survey responses as including each facility's physical location, regional water planning area, contracted and actual electrical load, and water intake and sources, stated by the petitioner rather than verified
Sec. 552.325 entitles a requestor to intervene in a suit seeking to withhold information and requires notice to the requestor
